hook_text: For a hundred years, the Xhosa fought to keep their land. Nine wars. Here's why.
clip_script: The Zuurveld, 1770s: Xhosa cattle farmers and trekboer cattle farmers need the same grass and water. Raids, reprisals, borders drawn on maps nobody agreed to. In 1812 the British drive twenty thousand Xhosa across the Fish River. In 1819 the prophet Makhanda leads thousands against Grahamstown, but cannons win the day. In 1835 King Hintsa comes to negotiate and is shot dead. War after war, the colony takes more land. By 1879, Xhosa independence is gone. Today, Makhanda, Hintsa and Maqoma are remembered as heroes of resistance.
visual_style: An animated map of the Eastern Cape with rivers labelled; the colonial border jumps east war by war; portraits sketched of Makhanda, Hintsa and Maqoma.
pacing: War by war, with pauses at key moments.
